raw_response:
My reasoning:

I am 49, been working this land for 30 years. My three mu is small, so I must think carefully about every yuan. My husband and my older boy work in the town most of the year, so the farm is mostly me and my mother-in-law when she is well enough. That means I cannot take on too much heavy work alone.

I will split my land like I always do. Two mu I plant wheat in autumn and then maize right after the wheat comes off in June — that is how everyone around here does it, two crops on the same land. One mu I keep for cotton. Cotton is hard work, lots of spraying and picking, but the price is better and I have been doing it many years so I know it.

For wheat, I buy one bag of compound fertilizer (that big 50 jin bag) per mu when I plant in October, and then when the wheat greens up in spring I spread about half a bag of urea. My neighbor Auntie Wang does the same and her wheat is good. I water once before winter, once in spring when it jointing, and once more if the sky does not give rain before the grain fills. I spray once for the aphids when I see them. Usually I get four, maybe four and half hundred jin per mu — that is 450 kg — if the weather is kind.

For maize after wheat, I just push the seed in, no ploughing, save the tractor money. One bag of compound when I plant and one bag of urea when it is knee-high. One watering usually enough because summer has rain. One spray for the borer. I get around 550 kg, sometimes 600 if rain comes right.

For cotton on the one mu, I have to work harder. I plough that mu in spring, put in two bags of compound fertilizer because cotton is hungry, and then one bag of urea when flowers come. I water two or three times. The bollworm is bad so I spray four or five times — this is expensive but if I skip it I lose everything. I expect about 250 kg seed cotton.

I use improved seed for wheat like my neighbors, hybrid maize seed from the dealer in town (everyone uses hybrid now), and Bt cotton seed because the bollworm spray alone would eat all my profit otherwise.
